final.memo:
We have initiated a position in the Company, a leading seller of nutritional and weight-management products, which we believe is currently mispriced by a public short-seller campaign [D01, D03, D05]. While the market fears that the company’s business model is a pyramid scheme susceptible to regulatory collapse, we see a highly cash-generative enterprise being sacrificed to the fears of the moment [D03, D05].

The math is compelling: the company trades at 9.88x trailing P/E, a steep discount compared to peers like Nu Skin, which trades at 17.8x [D04]. Based on annualized Q3 2012 EPS of $4.16 and an adjusted peer multiple, we see a path to a $69.16 valuation, representing significant upside from current levels [D03, D04].

The market’s focus on short-seller allegations has created a disconnect between the company’s strong underlying cash generation—evidenced by $142.4m in operating cash flow in Q3 2012—and its depressed equity valuation [D03, D04]. We expect this valuation gap to close as the regulatory environment clarifies and the business model’s legality is defended [D03, D07].

Our role here is as an opportunistic investor monitoring an event-driven inflection point [D07]. We require no board changes or management restructuring at this time, preferring to let the fundamental cash generation drive a market-led correction [D03, D07]. Should regulatory findings confirm the short-seller thesis, we will exit the position immediately [D03, D05].

We have sized this as a 5% position. We view the downside floor at $25.00, assuming the business maintains its current cash-flow-generative trajectory following regulatory clearance [D03, D04, D05]. We are prepared to move quickly if the catalyst of regulatory resolution breaks in either direction [D03, D05, D07].
